design.decision: After making the contract, choose freely: trump to set the opponents, or discard winners to avoid overtricks.
design.opponent: Revealed the first time it allows a play that would otherwise be illegal. Opponents then expect trumps from an apparently long hand.
design.rationale: This gives the dead tricks after a make a purpose, which helps the lopsided endgame the brief describes. It is a stronger Exact enabler than seed-any-suit's fixed last three tricks. One condition, one effect.
design.draftText: Your team can play any suit once your team has won the tricks in its contract
design.hooks: Generalize anySuit with a condition field: the follow-suit exemption switches on once the owning team's non-nil bidders have won tricks equal to the contract. The same field could later support other trick-count conditions.

critic.concerns: Clean, visible switch-on condition with clear counterplay; 'won the tricks in its contract' should make clear that tricks a nil bidder wins don't count.
